Now I understand the `fill` function. It processes escaped characters. So when the input has `@include \"`, the WORD token would be `\"` (backslash + quote), and `fill` would convert it to just `"` (a single double-quote character).

So the input `@include \"\n` would produce a WORD token that is just `"` (a single double-quote character). Then in `expand_include`, `*opath == '"'` is true, so it does `olen -= 2`. Since `olen` is 1 (the length of `"`), this underflows to a huge value.

Let me verify this by looking at the `fill` function implementation. Let me find where it's defined.

<parameter=command>grep -rn "fill" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/sudo/plugins/sudoers/toke.c | grep -v "sudoerslval\|sudoerstext\|sudoersleng\|LEXTRACE\|parser_leak\|yy_fill\|fill_buffer\|fill_args\|fill_cmnd" | head -20</｜｜DSML｜｜>
